findings.title: Unhandled exceptions during OAuth token exchange cause 500 instead of install error
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen, safe_urlread and get_user_info without any try/except around the network calls. If GitHub returns an error for a bad/re-used code, safe_urlopen raises, and get_user_info can also raise ApiError. The code only handles the case where payload lacks access_token, so the cases the PR description claims to handle (bad code, re-used code, user-info failure) will raise an unhandled exception and return 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page.

findings.title: Direct metadata['sender']['login'] access can KeyError and breaks old integrations
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. Integrations created before sender tracking, or where the webhook did not store sender, have no metadata sender key. That raises KeyError and turns a reinstall/repair into a 500 instead of the controlled error page. It must use safe .get() access and treat a missing sender as a verification failure.

findings.title: New-install path skips authenticated-user verification
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.DoesNotExist, without comparing github_authenticated_user to anything. Only the branch where an Integration row already exists (created by the webhook with sender info) performs the attacker-vs-installer check. A fresh installation_id that has no Integration row yet therefore bypasses the security check this PR is supposed to add and proceeds to build the integration.
